A church was built after their names in the village of el-Sawamaa Sharq (east) about ten kilometers north east of Akhmeem. Their bodies are located beside the body of their uncle Anba Psote (Bisada) the martyred bishop of Psoi (Absai) in his monastery located twenty-five kilometers south of Akhmeem.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
The Departure of Pope Anastasius, the 36th Patriarch of Alexandria

On this day also of the year 332 of the martyrs (616 A.D.) the Holy Father Pope Anastasius, the 36th Pope of Alexandria, departed. He was educated in the School of Alexandria and worked as a judge in the royal court. Then he left his position and was ordained a priest for the church of Alexandria.

The believers increased their appreciation for him, honored, and truly loved him for what they saw of sincerity, wisdom and uprightness in him. All these characteristics were the best recommendation for him to be chosen patriarch after the departure of Pope Demianos.

After his consecration, he devoted a great attention for the church. He ordained many bishops and priests to fill the vacant posts. He built several new churches and regained the churches that were being taken over by the Chalcedonians. The Chalcedonian Patriarch was annoyed so he falsely accused him to the Emperor. The Emperor sent his orders to the Governor of Alexandria to seize some of the churches that under the auspices of the Patriarch Anastasius and to hand them over to the alien patriarch.

Pope Anastasius was saddened and went to the wilderness of Shiheet where he stayed for many days in fasting and prayers asking for divine intervention. Subsequently the emperor’s brother killed him and took over the throne. Pope Anastasius returned to Alexandria and persisted in teaching and exhorting the flock in person and through his books.

Because of his great knowledge and eloquence, he wrote a book every year. He remained on the patriarchal throne for twelve years during which he wrote twelve books and arranged them according to the Coptic alphabets as their titles. When he completed his good endeavor he departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
8-6: The Departure of St. Mary of Egypt, the Anchorite

On this day of the year 137 of the martyrs (421 A.D.) the hermit St. Mary of Egypt departed. She was born in the city of Alexandria about the year 61 of the martyrs (345 A.D.) to Christian parents. When she became 12 years old, Satan the enemy of good, deceived her and through her, he caught innumerable souls in doing evil.

She continued in this sinful life for 17 years until the grace of God touched her life. She met people from Alexandria going to Jerusalem so she went with them. She also went on her sinful life there. Until one day she wished to enter through the door of the church of Resurrection, but she felt a power preventing her from entering the church and that was repeated for several times. Right away she realized that, what was happening because of her corruption.

She lifted up her eyes with a broken heart before the icon of the Virgin St. Mary she wept and interceded with her for the Lord to forgive her sins. She confirmed her strong intention of leaving the life of sin and the world totally. Then she entered the church without any hindrance. She wept profusely and rejoiced for the acceptance of her repentance. She entreated God to guide her for what was pleasing to Him and to guide her new life.

She stood before the icon of the blessed Virgin St. Mary and asked for her intercession. She heard a voice coming out of the icon saying: "If you cross the Jordan River you will find rest and salvation." She left the church after she had confessed and partaken of the Holy Mysteries. When she left the church and on her way she met a man who gave her three silver coins with which she bought bread. Then she crossed the Jordan River to the wilderness where she dwelt for 17 years fighting the lusts and the evil desires. She fought as she was fighting against real beasts until she overcame the enemy with the grace of God. She sustained herself with the herbs and plants of the desert.

In the forty fifth year of her seclusion St. Zosima went to the wilderness, according to the custom of the monks of Palestine during the holy great fast for devotion and asceticism. Near the end of the fast he saw on his way back this Saint from far and he thought that she was a phantom. She fled from him however he ran after her until she hid herself behind a rock. She talked to him saying: "O my father Zosima, forgive me, if you wish to talk to me, throw me something to cover myself for I am naked." He marveled for she called him by his name. He threw to her his cloak and she covered herself with it. She asked him to bless her for he was a priest. He was amazed for she knew of his priesthood and instead he asked her to bless him. He asked her about her life story. She told him about all what had happened to her and asked him to go back to his monastery and not to tell anyone about her. She also asked him to bring with him in the next year the Holy Eucharist to partake of it.

In the next year she met him by the Jordan River and he was standing on the western shore of the river. She made the sign of the cross and walked over the water to the western shore. He marveled at that and she partook of the Holy Mysteries. She asked him to come to her in the next year. When he came to her in the following year Fr. Zosima found that she had departed while she was kneeling so he prayed over her. He found beside her a writing saying “My father Zosima, bury the body of Mary, the wretched woman, and leave to the dust this sinful body, and pray on my behalf." After he had buried her, he returned to his monastery, and told the monks her blessed biography. The Holy Father St. Zosima visited her cave every year. All the years of her life were 76 years spent 47 of them in the wilderness.

The blessing of her prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen
8-7: The Departure of the Righteous St. Joachim, the Father of the Blessed Virgin St. Mary

On this day the just man St. Joachim the father of the blessed Virgin St. Mary, departed. He was born in the city of Nazareth, a descendant of King David and of the tribe of Judah.

His wife Hannah was barren, and they both prayed and entreated God continually to give them a child. God gave them a good fruit which is the Virgin St. Mary. After God had pleased him with the birth of St. Mary, he presented her to the temple to serve as he vowed. He departed in peace at an age of 80 years when the Virgin was three years old.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.

On this day also the saint Anba Macrobius, the son of the governor of the city of Kaw, departed. When Anba Severus, Patriarch of Antioch, was wandering around the cities of Upper Egypt, he came to the city of Kaw and Macrobius ministered unto him. He accompanied Anba Severus on his visit to the monastery of Anba Moises. From what Macrobius saw from the holiness of the monks and their asceticism made him ask Anba Moises to accept him as a monk. Anba Moises explained to him the hardships of the monastic life.

Anba Moises asked him to resign his position and to relinquish all his money and possessions. He went to Kaw, appointed his brother in his place, returned to the monastery and put on the monastic garb. When his brothers Paul, Elias, and Joseph saw what their brother had done, they came to him and became monks by the hand of Anba Moises.

Anba Macrobius built many monasteries. There were about a thousand monks and about a thousand nuns under his guidance. He built many places for the poor and the needy, also built many churches and monasteries. God granted St. Macrobius the gift of healing the sick.

When Pope Theodosius, 33rd Patriarch, heard of him, he wrote praising and encouraging him. He asked him to come for the people of Alexandria could receive his blessing. When he came the Pope ordained him a priest then he returned to his monastery.

After he finished his good strife, he departed in peace. Multitudes gathered from all the nearby cities and his brother Anba Yousab, who was appointed as his successor in running the monasteries prayed over his brother Anba Macrobius and buried him.

The appearance of his body was on the seventh day of Tobe, seven hundred thirty three years after his departure. That was in the days of Anba Yousab, bishop of Akhmeem and the Archon Isaac the scribe of prince Eiz-Eldeen El-Hamawy. Anba Yousab took the body out of its tomb in the mountain, down to the church of the monastery, where they buried him with hymns and praises.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
The Martyrdom of Sts. Agapius and Theodora

On this day also is the commemoration of the martyrdom of Sts. Agapius and Theodora.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
8-8: The Martyrdom of the Holy Virgins: Agape, Eirene, and Shiona

On this day of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) the three holy virgins: Agape, Eirene, and Shiona were martyred. They were natives of Thessalonica, and worshipped the Lord Christ as their parents. They chose the life of chastity and vowed themselves to the Lord Christ. They persevered in fasting and praying, visited the convents often and practiced asceticism along with the nuns.

When Maximianus reigned, he restored the worship of idols and persecuted the Christians. These saints were afraid and they fled to the mountain and hid themselves in a cave devoting themselves to their worship and asceticism.

An old Christian woman visited them weekly to bring them food and take the work of their hands to sell it, and donated the remainder as alms on their behalf to the poor. One day a wicked person observed the frequent visits of this old woman to the mountain, so he followed her secretly until he knew the cave that she entered. He hid himself so she would not see him on her way back, for he thought that she was hiding precious things in it. After she left the cave he entered it and found the precious pearls the brides of Christ standing praying. He informed the governor of Thessalonica about them. When they stood before the governor they confessed a good confession and refused to offer sacrifices to the gods. The Governor became furious, severely tortured them, then cast them into the fire thus they received the crowns of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
The Martyrdom of the 150 believers by the hand of king of Persia

On this day also is the commemoration of the martyrdom of one hundred and fifty of the believers by the hand of the king of Persia. This king besieged Christian cities which were nearby the borders of his country, and captured many of the Christians. When they refused to worship the sun and the stars, he commanded to behead them thus they received the crowns of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
8-9: The Departure of St. Zosima (Zosimus) the Priest

On this day of the year 141 of the martyrs (425 A.D.) the ascetic Holy Father Abba Zosima the priest, departed. He was born in the year 326 A.D. to godly Christian parents, who were natives of Palestine. When he was five years old his parents handed him to a righteous old monk, who raised him up in a Christian manner and taught him the church subjects. Shortly after he was ordained a deacon, then he became a righteous monk and grew in virtues.

He devoted himself to praising God and reading the Holy Scriptures day and night and during work also. When he had completed thirty five years in the monastery he was ordained a priest. Accordingly he increased his ascetic labors and spiritual struggle.

After spending thirteen years in the priesthood the enemy of good sowed in his mind that he surpassed all his contemporaries in virtues and righteousness. But the mercy of God willed to turn him away from this thought. God sent him an angel who commanded him to go to the monastery which was nearby the Jordan River. He rose up and went to the monastery where he found therein holy old men who were perfect in their way of life. He realized that he was far from what he thought of himself and he stayed with them.

The custom of these monks during the Holy Lent; after they partook of the Holy Communion on the first Sunday of the fast, they left the monastery. They wandered in the desert of Jordan each one carried out his spiritual fight by himself. St. Zosimus used to go out with them each year wandering in the desert asking God to show him what was profitable for him.

One day as he was wandering about he encountered St. Mary the Egyptian (Coptic). He learned from her about her life story and the reason for her wandering in the desert. She told him and asked him to visit her in the next year and to bring her the Holy Mysteries. In the following year he found that she had departed. He prayed over her and buried her. When he returned he told the monks of the monastery her life story and her spiritual strife. He lived ninety nine years then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
The commemoration of the Sign that took place by the hands of Pope Shenouda I, 55th Patriarch of Alexandria

On this day also of the year 582 of the martyrs (866 A.D.) a great sign took place by the hands of our holy father Pope Shenouda I, 55th Patriarch of Alexandria. This honorable father had an annual custom to go to the monastery of St. Macarius to spend the Passion Week in the monastery.

On one occasion, after celebrating the Holy Covenant Thursday liturgy, the monks returned to their cells. At that moment, the barbarians attacked them, pelting them with stones. The monks fled back to the Pope to inform him of what had happened. The Pope comforted them with words of grace. Then, taking his staff, which bore the sign of the cross, the Pope went out to meet the barbarians, saying, "It is better for me to die with the people of God." When the barbarians saw him coming out alone, unarmed, they retreated before his extraordinary courage, as if soldiers had driven them away from that place, and they never returned with evil intent from that day on.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
8-10: The Departure of Anba Isaac, the Disciple of Anba Apollo

On this day the Holy Father Anba Isaac the disciple of the great Anba Apollo, departed. This holy man renounced the world since his young age. He became a monk in the wilderness of Shiheet (Scetis) under the guidance of Anba Apollo for twenty-five years. He exerted himself with a strenuous spiritual fight.

He mastered the virtue of silence and quietness especially during the prayers and the Liturgies. He used to stand during the liturgy with his hands clasped and his head bent down until the end of the prayer then he returned to his cell, shutting his door, and did not associate with any one that day. When they asked him: "Why do you not talk to anyone who wished to talk to you during prayers or the Liturgy?" He answered saying: "There is time for talking and there is time for praying."

When his departure drew near the fathers the monks gathered around him to receive his blessing and they asked him: "Why did you flee from men." He answered them: "I was not fleeing from men but from Satan. For if a man hold a lighted lamp in the wind, it will be extinguished. So, it is with us when our minds enlightened during the prayers and the Liturgy then we occupy ourselves by talking with each other, our minds become darkened."

When he finished his good endeavor departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
The Departure of Pope Gabriel II, 70th patriarch of Alexandria, known as Ibn Turayk

On this day also of the year 861 of the martyrs (1145 A.D.) the Holy Father Pope Gabriel II, 70th Patriarch of Alexandria, who was known as Ibn Turayk, departed. This saint was born in Old Cairo in the year 800 of the martyrs (1084 A.D.). His father was a pious priest who raised him with a Christian upbringing. His name was Abu el-Alaa Sa-eid Ibn Turayk and was ordained a deacon at a young age. He was wise, loving to everyone, well versed in the Holy Scriptures and the religious subjects.

Abu el-Alaa was also a scribe in the court of el-Khalifa. After a while he wanted to devote himself to serve the church of the martyr Abu Saifain however the Khalifa allowed him on condition of keeping his position as a scribe.

In the later days of Pope Macarius, someone working in the court of el-Khalifa falsely accused the Copts before him that they take the revenue of the churches and pass it on to the Europeans in secret. El-Khalifa became angry and ordered to take the revenue of the churches to the treasury. For this reason the Copts did not dare to take permission to elect a new Patriarch. They waited about two years until those accused the Copts were killed and the affairs had quieted down. Subsequently el-Khalifa permitted them to elect a new Patriarch.

A group of people went to the wilderness of St. Macarius where they met Anba Youssef the abbot of St. John Kama’s monastery who told them; “Return O my children to Miser (Cairo) for the one who is chosen from God is the deacon Abu al-Alaa Ibn Turayk.” They returned to Cairo and took Abu Alaa to Alexandria. He was consecrated on the 9th of Meshir, year 847 of the martyrs (1131 A.D.). He was forty seven years old and was called Gabriel II.

After the enthronement he went to St. Macarius monastery in Shiheet where he celebrated the Divine Liturgy. At the end of the Liturgy, he added to the confession this sentence "He made it one with His Divinity.” When the fathers objected he informed them that this statement was added by the Holy Synod. After a lengthy deliberation, they asked him to add this sentence: "Without mingling, without confusion, and without alteration," because of the fear of falling into the heresy of Eutyches, and the Pope agreed with them.

During his papacy, he ordained 53 bishops and many priests. He completely refused simony for ordinations.

Pope Gabriel had many splendid achievements, of them:

First: He commanded the reading of the epistles and the Gospels in Arabic after reading them in Coptic, also the sermons so that the people could understand the readings and the sermons.

Second: The Pope realized the difficulty of reading the Holy Bible, the two testaments, in Passion Week. He arranged certain readings for that purpose then Anba Peter (Petros) bishop of El-Bahnasa added the proper prophecies and sermons for each hour to form the Katameros (Lectionary) of the Holy Pascha which the Church still uses today.

Anba Peter also arranged for the four Gospels to be read during the Passion Week: the gospel of St. Matthew on Tuesday, the gospel of St. Mark on Wednesday, the gospel of St. Luke on Thursday and the gospel of St. John to be read in the eve of the Holy Resurrection.

He also arranged the reading of the one hundred fifty one psalms, in the eve of bright Saturday.

Third: Pope Gabriel issued some canons in three books:

First Book: it contained thirty two canons concerning the organization of the affairs of the church, and the civil and religious relation of the people with the church.

Second Book: Was about the organization of all things concerning the clergy.

Book Three: Was about inheritance.

After this saint had completed his good endeavor he had a serious illness. During his sickness, he saw in a dream a group of priests and monks carrying gospels, censers and crosses and heard them saying; “You will be healed, however we will come back to you after one year to take you to be with us.” He was cured and after one year he departed in peace. He remained on the Apostolic Throne for fourteen years and three months.

He was buried in the church of the martyr St. Mercurius Abu Saifain. During the papacy of Pope Marcus III, 73rd Patriarch of Alexandria, the body of Pope Gabriel II was relocated along with the body of Anba Youannes V to the monastery of St. Macarius in Shiheet. That was during the Holy Fast of the year 1170 A.D. in a great celebration.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
8-12: The Commemoration of the Honorable Archangel Michael

On this day of every Coptic month the church celebrates a commemoration for the honorable Archangel Michael the head of the heavenly hosts and the intercessor of mankind.

The blessing of his holy intercession be with us all. Amen
The Departure of St. Alexander, the Confessor, Bishop of Jerusalem

On this day also of the year 250 A.D. the Holy Father Anba Alexander, the confessor, bishop of Jerusalem, departed. He was a fellow student of the scholar Origen in the Theological School of Alexandria. He studied at the hands of St. Pantaenus and his successor St. Clement of Alexandria, and he grew in virtue and knowledge.

This Holy Father was chosen a bishop for one of the cities of Cappadocia. In the year 202 A.D., he confessed the Lord Christ before Emperor Septimius Severus who seized, tortured and imprisoned him for many years. After his release and with divine providence he went to Jerusalem to receive the blessing of the holy places and then return to his country.

St. Narcissus, who was the Bishop of Jerusalem at that time, was advanced in age. When St. Alexander finished his visit and decided to return to his diocese in Cappadocia, the people of Jerusalem heard a voice from heaven saying: "Go to the gate of the city, and the first one to enter it, seize him and make him stay with St. Narcissus to assist him." When they went to the gate they met the Bishop Alexander, and they pleaded with him to stay with Abba Narcissus to assist him. He refused because he could not leave his flock that the Lord Christ had entrusted him with. They told him about the voice which they heard and that it was God's Will. He accepted and wrote to the people of his parish. He remained in Jerusalem, assisting its bishop Anba Narcissus, for about 3 years.

After the departure of St. Narcissus, he continued to shepherd the people of Jerusalem with the best of care. In the year 216 A.D. the scholar Origen went to Palestine and his old friend Alexandros welcomed him. He ordained him a priest what displeased Pope Demetrius the vine dresser, 12th Patriarch of Alexandria.

Emperor Maximianus seized St. Alexander, inflicted him with many tortures and then imprisoned him. When Emperor Gordian III reigned, he released the saint. This father sat on the Episcopal throne in quietness and peace until Decius rose, killed Emperor Philip, and reigned in his stead.

When Decius incited persecution against the Christians; he seized this Holy Father and many other believers and tortured them severely. He cast St. Alexander in prison where he remained until he departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
The Departure of St. Antonios, Bishop of Thmoui

On this day also was the departure of the Holy Father St. Antonios, Bishop of Thmoui.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
13-6:
Come all you faithful people, who have been bought by the pure Blood of our Lord, and Savior Jesus Christ. Let us glorify Him for what He bestowed upon us from His benevolence, goodness, and abundantly gave us from His blessings and richness. He brought us to this day, which is the last day of the Coptic year, and we are physically healthy, steadfast in our faith, and following the way of the Lord with the blessing of our holy fathers.

We greatly thank God for He did not deal with us according to our bad deeds but He lingered on us, and kept us, to this day, in peace, awaiting our return to Him in repentance, so that he might grant us forgiveness.

Let us repent from all our hearts for all that we had committed, from iniquities and trespasses, and let us weep shedding our tears before him for the transgressions and sins that we have committed. Let us commit ourselves before Him to live pure and chaste lives. We ask Him to establish us in the True Faith, to preserve us from the snare of Satan, to grant us His perfect peace that surpasses every mind, and to repose the souls of our departed ones with the intercession of the Virgin Lady St. Mary, and all the choir of the angels, the pure apostles, the martyrs and all the saints who pleased God with their good deeds.

Glory, Honor, and Worship to Our God now and ever and unto the ages of the ages. Amen.

Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.
Liturgy
Pauline Epistle

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the Second Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Corinthians. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint Peter. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 20th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Toubah.

Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Hebrews. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the Third Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 3rd of the Blessed Coptic Month of Baounah.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Martyrdom of St. Alladius the Bishop
The Departure of St. Abraam, Bishop of El Fayyom
The Departure of the Ascetic St. Martha of Egypt
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 3rd of the Blessed Coptic Month of Toubah.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Martyrdom of the Children of Bethlehem
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint Matthew the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the  Epistle of Saint James. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 15th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Amshir.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Departure of St. Paphnoute, the Monk
The Martyrdom of the Righteous Zechariah the Prophet the Son of Berechiah, the Son of Iddo
The Martyrdom of Anba Begoul (Pigol) the Priest
The Consecration of the First Church Dedicated for the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint Matthew the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 20th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Baramoudah.
May God end it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Martyrdom of St. Babnuda (Paphnute) of Dendereh
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.
Liturgy
Pauline Epistle

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the First Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Corinthians. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Hebrews. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 28th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Bashans.
May God end it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Commemoration of the Relocation of the Body of St. Epiphanius, Bishop of Cyprus
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint Peter. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 2nd of the Blessed Coptic Month of Amshir.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Departure of the Great Saint Anba Paul, the First Hermit
The Departure of St. Longinus, Abbot of El-Zugag Monastery and his father St. Lucianus
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.
Liturgy
Pauline Epistle
Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 29th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Baramoudah.

Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint Luke the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.

Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 15th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Bashans.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Martyrdom of St. Simon the Zealot (Simon the Canaanite), one of the Twelve Apostles
The Martyrdom of 400 martyrs in Dandara (Denderah)
The Martyrdom of the Hermit St. Mina the Deacon
The Departure of the Priest Shams El-Ri'asah Abi El-Barakat known as Ebn Kabr
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint Luke the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.
Liturgy
Pauline Epistle

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Hebrews. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint Peter. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the Second Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Thessalonians. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 14th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Bashans.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Departure of St. Pachomius (Pakhom), the Father of the Spiritual Communal Monastic life (Cenobitic life)
The Martyrdom of St. Epimachus (Ephimachus) of Pelusium
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.
Liturgy
Pauline Epistle

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Colossians. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 7th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Baramoudah.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.

Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint Peter. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 27th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Amshir.
May God end it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Departure of St. Eustathius, Patriarch of Antioch
The Martyrdom of St. Perpetua and her Companions
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint Luke the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the First Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Corinthians. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the Third Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 7th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Baounah.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Martyrdom of St. Abaskhiroun of Qalin, the Soldier
The Departure of St. Moises of Akhmim Mount
The Consecration of the church of St. Matthew (Mettaos) el-Fakhory in Esna Mount
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Ephesians. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 20th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Toubah.
May God end it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Departure of St. Prochorus, One of the Seventy Disciples
The Martyrdom of Anba Kloag (Bagoug), the Priest
The Martyrdom of St. Behna (Bahnou)
The Commemoration of the Consecration of the Church of St. John, the Owner of the Golden Gospel
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint Matthew the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.
Liturgy
Pauline Epistle
Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint Matthew the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint Matthew the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.
Liturgy
Pauline Epistle
Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 4th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Bashans.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.

From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the  Epistle of Saint James. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 26th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Baramhat.
May God end it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Departure of St. Euphrasia (Eupraxia), the virgin
The Departure of Pope Peter VI, 104th Patriarch of Alexandria
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 17th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Bashans.
May God end it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Departure of St. Epiphanius, Bishop of Cyprus
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint Peter. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 5th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Baounah.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
The Departure of St. James the Oriental, the Confessor
The Martyrdom of St Bifam
The Martyrdom of Sts. Anba Bishay (Ebsoy) and Anba Botros (Peter)
The Consecration of the church of St. Boctor (Victor) in the region of Sho
Psalm & Gospel
Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint Luke the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.
Liturgy
Pauline Epistle

Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Colossians. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.

Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint Luke the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.
Liturgy
Pauline Epistle
Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the First Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 1st of the Blessed Coptic Month of Baounah.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.

Stand in the fear of God and listen to the Holy Gospel. A reading from the Holy Gospel according to our teacher Saint John the Evangelist. May His Blessings be with us all. Amen.
From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and the king, may his blessings be with us all. Amen.
Alleluia
Blessed is he who comes in the Name of the Lord. Our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ, Son of the Living God, unto Him be the glory forever, Amen.
Glory be to God forever.

Liturgy
Pauline Epistle
Paul, the servant of our Lord Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, appointed to the Gospel of God. A reading from the  Epistle of our teacher Paul to the Romans. May his blessings be with us. Amen.
The grace of God the Father be with you all. Amen.
Catholic Epistle
A Reading from the Second Epistle of Saint John. May his blessings be upon us. Amen.
Do not love the world or the things in the world. The world passes away, and its desires; but he who does the will of God abides forever. Amen.
Acts of the Apostles
The Acts of our fathers the apostles, may their blessings be with us. Amen.
The word of the Lord shall grow, multiply, be mighty, and be confirmed, in the holy Church of God. Amen.
Synaxarium

In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit One God. Amen
Day 12th of the Blessed Coptic Month of Baounah.
May God begin it in goodness and renew it for us in peace and tranquility, while our sins and iniquities are forgiven through the tender mercies of our Lord, O my fathers and my brethren. Amen.
